decisions.statement: The change to repeat is named by the first word of the call.
`at-most` says how many pages one batch acts on.
A batch is a run of `akasha change apply` and is judged by the checks as any apply is.
A call naming neither a change nor the help flag is refused.
The help flag is answered with what a repeat does and what a repeat takes.
The help flag is read before the arguments are, so nothing need be piped in.
A change whose page states no `takes-at-most` is refused.
A call handed no `at-most` is refused.
A ceiling that is no whole number above nothing is refused.
Whether a change takes a ceiling is read off that change's page.
Every batch is handed the arguments the call was piped, unchanged.
A batch runs in a child of its own rather than in this process.
The file a child runs is read from the index rather than spelled here.
A batch that landed a commit is followed by another batch.
A batch landing no commit ends the run.
The edits a batch landing no commit left kept are dropped.
A drop that refused is said with what ended the run.
A call made where edits are kept already lands those edits before its first batch.
Edits that will not land refuse the call rather than being dropped.
That refusal says why the landing refused rather than that edits are kept.
A row that reads as no edit is swept rather than refusing the call.
What the opening landing did is reported and counted as no batch.
What that batch said is the last thing the report says.
A run whose first batch landed nothing is refused rather than answered as done.
The report names the commit each batch landed.
Each batch is named as soon as that batch has committed.
A run that threw part way names those batches in its refusal.
No line a batch printed of what it wrote is carried into the report.
This command edits nothing itself.
No ceiling is held on how many batches one run takes.

definition: the command applying one change batch after batch until a batch lands nothing
